sanskrit: satyābhisamaye ṣoḍaśabhirbhavāgravairāgye cāṣṭādaśabhirnavaprakārāṇāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya navānantaryavimuktimārgotpādanāt / ta ete catustriṃśat bhavanti / ākiñcanyāyatanavītarāgasyāsyaniyāmāvakramaṇādadhobhūmikā na punaḥḥ praheyā bhavanti /
english: The School admits in fact that the Bodhisattva obtains Bodhi in thirty-four moments, namely sixteen moments that constitute the “comprehension of the Truths” and eighteen moments that constitute the abandoning of the defilements relative to Bhavāgra, ie. , nine āṉantaryamārgas and nine vimuktimārgas. The eighteenth moment is kṣayajñāna. These thirty-four moments suffice, for, before entering into the “comprehension of the Truths,” the Bodhisattva, still a Prṛthagjana, detaches himself through the worldly path from all spheres, with the exception of Bhavāgra. The eighteen moments form a path during the course of which the Saint does not produce a mind of a different nature, that is, a worldly, impure mind, for example the mind entering the absorption of extinction.
